REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 27, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
SEPTEMBER 27, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery, The Church of Jesus
  Christ of the Latter-Day Saints.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Elijah Granflor, Recreation Services Division
  Youth Sports League Scorekeeper.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  A Proclamation was given to:

  Sunset Industrial Parts (Business Spotlight)

  The City Council presented a City of Cerritos Commission service plaque to the
  family, husband Pradeep and daughter Astha, of late Fine Arts and Historical
  Commission member Smita Das.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Daisy Lagasca expressed her appreciation for the Cerritos on Wheels (COW)
  drivers and the assistance they provide for Cerritos residents. She announced the
  upcoming e-waste event at Cerritos High School and spoke regarding Measure
  BB on the November ballot.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding the United Homeowners Alliance and their opposition
  to Measure BB. He encouraged the community to vote “no” on Measure BB.

  Ernie Nishii expressed support for the information technology infrastructure
  required to support instruction and security in the school district.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke regarding domestic security issues.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  August 23, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 23, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September
  27, 2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to approve the Register
  of Demands as follows:

  7B.1. City of Cerritos  9/27/2018 $7,938,352.29 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the
  period ending August 31, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending August
  31, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  Receive and file the 2018 Local Agency Biennial Notice, pursuant to the Political
  Reform Act of 1974, directing the proposed amendments to be returned to the
  City Council and appropriate agencies at the first meeting of December 2018
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Receive and file the 2018 Local Agency Biennial Notice; and

  2.  Direct the City Clerk’s Office to present any proposed changes to the codes
  for review and adoption by the City Council and appropriate agencies at the
  first meeting in December (scheduled for December 13, 2018)
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of Bid No. 1346-18, Printing of the 2019 Cerritos Community Calendar
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to award Bid No. 1346-
  18 for the printing of the 2019 Cerritos Community Calendar to Meridian Graphics, in
  the amount of $19,595.03. In the event issues of non-performance arise, the project
  is to be removed from Meridian Graphics and taken to the next lowest bidder to
  ensure the City’s printing deadline, quality standards, and specifications are met
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7F.  Award of Bid No. 1344-18, Annual Water Mains and Appurtenances for Repairs
  and Services (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Award contracts for the Annual Water Mains and Appurtenances for Repairs and

  2.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 2018-8, A DEVELOPMENT PROPOSAL
  BY PROPERTY OWNER BEACHCOM, LLC, TO CONSTRUC A NEW SINGLE-TENANT,
  ONE-STORY COMMERCIAL BUILDING AND RELATED SITE AND LANDSCAPE
  IMPROVEMENTS ON A VACANT PARCEL LOCATED AT 13359 SOUTH STREET,
  CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED COMMUNITY
  COMMERCIAL (CC) (APN 7028-027-001) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15303 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Robert A. Lopez, Current Planning Manager.  A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Jonathan Matson, project architect, spoke regarding the project.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to adopt Resolution
  No. 2018-16, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING
  PRECISE PLAN 2018-8, A DEVELOPMENT PROPOSAL BY THE PROPERTY
  OWNER BEACHCOM, LLC, TO CONSTRUCT A NEW SINGLE-TENANT, ONE-
  STORY COMMERCIAL BUILDING AND RELATED SITE AND LANDSCAPE
  IMPROVEMENTS ON A VACANT PARCEL LOCATED AT 13359 SOUTH
  STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS
  ZONED COMMUNITY COMMERCIAL (CC) (APN 7028-027-001) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business
9A.  Review and consideration of the 2018 City Council/Successor Agency meeting
  schedule (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to cancel the Regular
  Meeting of the City Council/Successor Agency scheduled for Thursday, October
  11, 2018 and schedule a Special City Council/Successor Agency Meeting on
  Monday, October 8, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  September 27, 2018

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of a sole source contract for updating and
  maintaining the Water Division’s Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition
  (SCADA) System (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1.  Find that staff has satisfied the purposes of the bidding regulation of the
  City of Cerritos Municipal Code; and

  2.  Find that it is reasonable and necessary to sole source the Support and
  Maintenance of the SCADA system in accordance with Section 3.20.060 of
  the City of Cerritos Municipal Code; and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to enter into an annual contract
  with HSQ Technology, in the amount of $16,068 for supporting and
  maintaining the Water Division’s SCADA system for an initial term of two
  (2) years with an option to extend the contract for two (2) one (1) year
  extensions upon mutual agreement to the terms and conditions (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of approval of a utility agreement with the California
  Department of Transportation establishing the liability for the costs related to
  the relocation of streetlights on Valley View Avenue in connection with the I-5
  Corridor Improvement Project within the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to staff’s request, this item was continued to the next meeting of the
  City Council/Successor Agency.

9D.  Review and consideration of award of contracts for construction of
  improvements in residential streets (Project No. 14088) Bid No. 1348-18
  (asphalt), Bid No. 1349-18 (trees), and Bid No. 1350-18 (concrete) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  September 27, 2018

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to:
  1.  Award a contract in the amount of $376,835 for Construction of Asphalt
  Improvements in Residential Streets (total bid), Project No. 14088, Bid
  No. 1348-18, to Sequel Contractors and reject the other bids; and

  2.  Award a contract in the amount of $70,560 for the complete removal of 62
  parkway trees (total bid), Project No. 14088, Bid No. 1349-18, to Golden
  West Arborists and reject the other bids; and

  3.  Award a contract in the amount of $500,700 for Construction of Concrete
  Improvements in Residential Streets (total bid), Project No. 14088, Bid
  Nol. 1350-18, to CJ Concrete Construction and reject the other bids; and

  4.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1345-18, Supply of Compressed
  Liquid Chlorine (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Award a one-year contract, in the amount of $58,993, for the supply of
  compressed liquid chlorine, Bid No. 1345-18, to Thatcher Company of
  California and reject the other bid; and

  2.  With an option of three, one-year extensions, with mutual consent of both
  parties; and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  A presentation regarding the upcoming November 6, 2018 Statewide General
  Election was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk. A PowerPoint Presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Linda Johnson, Field Deputy for Supervisor Janice Hahn, Fourth District, was
  introduced and thanked for her contributions to the presentation.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor
  Pro Tem Solanki, and Mayor Pulido.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session to discuss any items.
